method: manual visual interpretation; not a calibrated pixel-perfect fit
notes: The side/front wall-span ratio is about 0.5; the earlier 9 m deep body was too deep.
Main roof rebuilt as a continuous pitched roof with timber gable ends above a lower hip skirt (irimoya), rather than a full hip.
The front timber feature is a closed, short ridge-mounted cross-gable; its infill, sill, bargeboards and ridge are modelled.
Roof height/pitch follow the drawing silhouette rather than the earlier 8 m envelope.
Hip tiles evaluate only their own skirt surface; they cannot bridge the vertical timber end and mask it.
Original views are design art; exact camera consistency is not asserted.

The prominent front/quarter timber triangle governs the cross-gable width and its mid-slope position; the right profile governs the actual main end gable. These design-art views are not a fully calibrated reconstruction.
